package_info.package_name: Midnight Blizzard (Cozy Bear) O365 Attack Chain
package_info.package_versions: N/A (targets legacy and test tenant accounts, not a software package version)
package_info.why_malicious: The attack chain leverages credential guessing, legacy account compromise, and abuse of OAuth applications to gain persistent, privileged access to corporate email and file environments, enabling stealthy exfiltration of sensitive data from high-value targets.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Automated password spray attack against legacy, non-product test tenant accounts using lists of common passwords.
malicious_snippets.code_language: N/A (attack technique, likely implemented in Python or PowerShell)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Before authentication, the attacker uses automated scripts to repeatedly attempt logins with common passwords against legacy test accounts, seeking weak credentials, resulting in unauthorized access if successful.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Password spraying is a brute-force technique designed to evade account lockout policies and target weakly protected accounts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal authentication attempts should originate from legitimate users and not involve repeated, automated login attempts across many accounts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Penetration testers may use password spraying with explicit authorization.
key_indicators: High volume of failed login attempts from a single IP
Targeting of legacy or test accounts

execution_context.file_location: Azure AD / Office 365 tenant (OAuth application configuration)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Compromise and abuse of a legacy test OAuth application with elevated access to the Microsoft corporate environment.
malicious_snippets.code_language: N/A (cloud configuration abuse, likely manipulated via PowerShell, Graph API, or Azure portal)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After gaining access, the attacker identifies and takes control of a legacy OAuth application with elevated permissions, using it to access Exchange Online mailboxes and exfiltrate sensitive emails.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Abuse of legacy OAuth applications is a known lateral movement and privilege escalation technique, often overlooked in cloud environments.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: OAuth applications should be tightly controlled and monitored; legacy or test apps should not have elevated permissions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate applications may use OAuth for automation, but not in a stealthy or unmonitored manner.
key_indicators: Access to high-value mailboxes via legacy OAuth apps
Unusual OAuth consent grants or privilege escalation
Access tokens issued to unexpected applications

execution_context.file_location: Exchange Online / SharePoint Online (cloud data stores)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Automated exfiltration of sensitive emails and SharePoint files from targeted accounts and repositories.
malicious_snippets.code_language: N/A (likely PowerShell, Graph API, or custom scripts)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After gaining mailbox and file access, the attacker systematically downloads and exfiltrates sensitive emails and files to external infrastructure under their control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated, targeted exfiltration of sensitive data is a hallmark of advanced persistent threat (APT) operations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal user or application behavior does not involve mass export of sensitive data from executive or security team mailboxes.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Data migration tools may perform similar actions, but with proper authorization and audit trails.
key_indicators: Bulk download/export of emails or files from high-value accounts
Data transfers to unfamiliar or foreign IP addresses
Access patterns inconsistent with user roles

attack_chain.action: Password spray attack against legacy test tenant accounts to gain initial access.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromise of a privileged account in the cloud environment.

attack_chain.action: Discovery and compromise of a legacy OAuth application with elevated permissions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Privilege escalation and persistent access to mailboxes and files.

attack_chain.action: Automated exfiltration of sensitive emails and SharePoint files from targeted accounts.
attack_chain.leads_to: Loss of sensitive data and potential further exploitation.

behavioral_signatures: Password spray attacks targeting legacy or test accounts
Unusual OAuth application privilege escalation or consent grants
Bulk mailbox or SharePoint file access from non-standard applications
Automated exfiltration of sensitive data from executive or security team accounts
file_indicators: Legacy OAuth application configurations with elevated permissions
Bulk export/download logs in Exchange Online or SharePoint
network_indicators: Outbound connections to unfamiliar or foreign IP addresses from cloud infrastructure
Unusual API calls to Microsoft Graph or Exchange Web Services from non-standard clients
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for high volumes of failed authentication attempts (password spraying), especially against legacy or test accounts. Audit OAuth application permissions and consent grants for privilege escalation. Alert on bulk mailbox or SharePoint file access, especially from applications or accounts not normally used for such operations. Correlate data exfiltration events with unusual network destinations and API usage patterns.
